llm_insights.narrative:
# Your 2025 Outside Memory

## Welcome Message

Hello Claudette! We're thrilled to celebrate your incredible engagement with Outside's community over the past eight months. As one of our most dedicated members, you've logged nearly 1,400 interactions across our properties—averaging over 6 visits per day. Your passion for outdoor adventure, endurance sports, and community is exactly what makes Outside thrive.

---

## Claudette's 2025 Outside Journey

Your year with us tells the story of a multi-sport athlete and adventure enthusiast who's deeply invested in both personal performance and the broader outdoor community. Starting in late January, you arrived with curiosity about wellness and travel—exploring treehouse retreats in Costa Rica and the best wellness destinations worldwide. But it quickly became clear that you're someone who doesn't just *read about* adventure; you *live it*.

As winter turned to spring, your engagement accelerated dramatically. March marked a turning point, with 152 events as you dove deeper into training content, race registration, and community activity feeds. This is when your patterns really emerged: you weren't just consuming content passively. You were sharing your own adventures—that beautiful day skiing with your favorite girl on #GetOutsideDay, capturing moments of natural beauty, and connecting with others doing the same. Your activity feed posts became windows into your world: sunrise moments, winter milestones, and the quiet joy of getting outside.

May and June became your peak months, with 246 and 357 events respectively. This surge coincided with what appears to be race season preparation and peak engagement with the cycling community. You explored gravel bike content with particular intensity—reading "Gravel Brands Are Failing Women Riders," diving into field tests for brands like Devinci, Lauf, and Specialized, and registering for events like The Ice Weasels Cometh. You were also consuming training wisdom voraciously: articles on physiological resilience, pre-race workouts from pros, and nutrition guidance for endurance athletes.

Throughout this journey, certain themes stayed constant: your deep love for skiing and winter sports, your commitment to endurance training across multiple disciplines, and your genuine investment in the outdoor community. Whether you were reading Lisa Jhung and Frederick Dreier on running and cycling, exploring Jen Murphy's wellness insights, or following the inspiring activity posts of fellow adventurers like Heather Dietrick and Rachel Risk, you were building a comprehensive picture of how to live an active, purposeful outdoor life.

---

## Your Passions

• **Endurance Sports & Racing** — With 145 interactions on BikeReg and multiple race registrations (Ice Weasels, Golden Nugget Criterium, Sunflower Relay), you're clearly an active competitor. Your reading spans training methodologies, nutrition for athletes, and gear reviews across cycling and running disciplines.

• **Gravel Cycling** — This emerged as a particular focus, with 5 dedicated gravel-related articles and deep dives into brand comparisons and field tests for gravel-specific equipment (Devinci, Lauf, Specialized, Stinner). You care about inclusivity in the sport, evidenced by your engagement with "Gravel Brands Are Failing Women Riders."

• **Winter Sports & Skiing** — Your activity posts celebrate winter milestones and snowy adventures. You completed the Intro to Skiing course and consistently engage with winter-specific content, from skate skiing stories to winter training strategies.

• **Nutrition & Performance Optimization** — With 13 food-related articles and 9 nutrition pieces consumed, you're methodical about fueling your athletic pursuits. You've read everything from "The Healthiest Costco Foods for Athletes" to "When Is the Best Time to Eat Breakfast?"—evidence of someone who understands that performance starts in the kitchen.

• **Adventure Travel & Exploration** — Your curiosity extends beyond your backyard. Costa Rican treehouses, Hawaii hiking safety, astronomy events, and wellness retreats all captured your attention. You're inspired by adventure but thoughtful about doing it responsibly.

• **Community & Storytelling** — Your engagement with activity feeds (116 home page visits) and your own posts reveal someone who values connection. You follow athletes like Heather Dietrick and Rachel Risk, celebrate others' moments, and share your own—creating a tapestry of shared outdoor experience.

---

## Your Reading Habits

Your reading patterns reveal someone with deliberate, purposeful engagement. You're most active in the evening hours—with peak activity at 9 PM (287 events), followed by 8 PM (194 events) and 10 PM (165 events). This suggests you're using Outside content to wind down, plan, and inspire before bed or during evening downtime. You're also a weekday reader, with Tuesday (341 events), Friday (284 events), and Thursday (283 events) dominating your engagement—likely fitting content consumption around work and training schedules. Weekends see a dramatic drop, suggesting you're actually *outside* rather than reading about it.

Your favorite authors tell a story of balanced interests. **Lisa Jhung** and **Frederick Dreier** (7 articles each) are your go-to voices—Jhung on running and wellness, Dreier on cycling culture and gear. **Jen Murphy** (6 articles) appears frequently, likely for her health and lifestyle expertise. You also regularly read **Betsy Welch** (5 articles), **Wes Siler** (4 articles), and **Ben Ayers** (4 articles), creating a trusted circle of voices across training, performance, and adventure.

What's striking is your breadth: you engage with 27 unique authors and 270 distinct articles across 97 different tags. You're not a one-topic reader. You move fluidly from "Embracing the Robot Overlords: My Experience with an AI Coach" (VeloNews) to "This Costa Rican Treehouse Hotel Elevated My Jungle-Adventure Expectations" to deep dives on search-and-rescue in Hawaii. Your reading is omnivorous but purposeful—every article seems to serve either your athletic development, your adventure planning, or your connection to the outdoor community.
